insights.topic: Deterministic purchase signals vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: 9,743 cryptographically verified receipts represent confirmed purchase events — not inferred intent. At a time when cookie deprecation is forcing brands back to probabilistic proxies, each of these signals carries a certainty premium the open ad market structurally cannot replicate.

The single largest GMV cycle on record added $56,064 in 4 hours on only 42 receipts — an average ticket north of $1,300 per receipt in that window. This signals that verified commerce data is capturing high-consideration purchases, not just convenience-store noise.

insights.topic: Category entropy as a cross-sell signal
insights.insight: At 3.262 bits of category entropy, no single vertical dominates — grocery, home improvement, electronics, restaurant, and now SaaS subscriptions coexist in the same verified signal pool. For brands seeking cross-category purchase attribution or basket-level insights, this diversity is structurally rare in deterministic data sets.

The first non-physical commerce category appeared in the network on April 9 — a meaningful inflection because it extends verified purchase signals beyond brick-and-mortar into recurring digital spend. Brands targeting software buyers or subscription-economy consumers now have a potential deterministic touchpoint that does not exist in retail media networks.

16 active CBSAs now include eight major metros — NYC, LA, Philadelphia, Boston, Seattle, Miami, Tampa, Pittsburgh — plus non-metro expansion into WA, OK, AL, ID, MI, RI, MA, and DC. The coverage map is beginning to match the DMA footprints that brand media plans are built around.

Token velocity rebounded to 1.037x even as two new CBSAs were added in the same cycle, suggesting new markets are generating repeat verified transactions faster than the prior 'thin new metros' pattern predicted. For marketers, this implies the signal density per market is approaching usable frequency thresholds sooner than expected.
